prompt:
Independently audit this contract against the indexed spec only.
Check (1) every spec segment mapped to a rule or marked unrelated/missing, (2) absent verbatim
evidence without uncertain, (3) contradictions between rule fields and examples, (4) plausible
alternative semantics with a concrete distinguishing chronological input sequence, and (5) derive
outputs for any explicit spec waveform/table/examples and compare. Report distinct material issues.
Return JSON {coverage:{Sxx:[rule IDs or "unrelated"/"missing"]},issues:[
{issue_id,rule_id (or "global"),type:"coverage"|"grounding"|"consistency"|"ambiguity"|"spec_example",
severity:"high"|"medium"|"low",detail,spec_evidence (verbatim spec or ""),alternative,sequence}]}.
Keep any deliberation brief and use short issue descriptions so the entire JSON fits. For ambiguity
the alternative must be specific; sequence must be a nonempty list of complete
width-valid nonclock input rows (optional mid) using the contract ports. For other types alternative
can be an empty string and sequence can be []. Code and prose outside JSON are not needed.
Indexed specification:
{"S01":"Build a gshare branch predictor with 7-bit pc and 7-bit global history, hashed (using xor) into a 7-bit index.","S02":"This index accesses a 128-entry table of two-bit saturating counters.","S03":"The branch predictor should contain a 7-bit global branch history register.","S04":"The branch predictor has two sets of interfaces: One for doing predictions and one for doing training.","S05":"The prediction interface is used in the processor's Fetch stage to ask the branch predictor for branch direction predictions for the instructions being fetched.","S06":"Once these branches proceed down the pipeline and are executed, the true outcomes of the branches become known.","S07":"The branch predictor is then trained using the actual branch direction outcomes.","S08":"// When a branch prediction is requested (predict_valid = 1) for a given pc, the branch predictor produces the predicted branch direction and state of the branch history register used to make the prediction.","S09":"The branch history register is then updated (at the next positive clock edge) for the predicted branch.","S10":"// When training for a branch is requested (train_valid = 1), the branch predictor is told the pc and branch history register value for the branch that is being trained, as well as the actual branch outcome and whether the branch was a misprediction (needing a pipeline flush).","S11":"Update the pattern history table (PHT) to train the branch predictor to predict this branch more accurately next time.","S12":"In addition, if the branch being trained is mispredicted, also recover the branch history register to the state immediately after the mispredicting branch completes execution.","S13":"// If training for a misprediction and a prediction (for a different, younger instruction) occurs in the same cycle, both operations will want to modify the branch history register.","S14":"When this happens, training takes precedence, because the branch being predicted will be discarded anyway.","S15":"If training and prediction of the same PHT entry happen at the same time, the prediction sees the PHT state before training because training only modifies the PHT at the next positive clock edge.","S16":"The following timing diagram shows the timing when training and predicting PHT entry 0 at the same time.","S17":"The training request at cycle 4 changes the PHT entry state in cycle 5, but the prediction request in cycle 4 outputs the PHT state at cycle 4, without considering the effect of the training request in cycle 4.","S18":"Reset is asynchronous active-high."}
